title: Drummers today versus New Orleans drummers; tuning drums
summary: Foster says current drummers are cymbal beaters, praises early New Orleans drummers and stresses tuning.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I got in rain with some guys around there. I said, you guys made a mistake buying drums. I said, man, you should all use some sticks and a cymbal beaters. Yeah. Yeah.

Yeah. None of them. See. Now, our voice drummers around New Orleans was better than some of the best ones that we had up there. See. And the one guy that was close to the New Orleans drummers, and he was very good, that was Sid Kaplan. Yeah. Well, he ran with Paul and those guys. Paul Bobbin was a very good drummer. But when I went home playing with his brother, I thought his brother was better drumming than him. He's just a little Bob. Yeah.
Good musical family. The whole family is good music.

See, Paul was very good. See, the average drummer up there don't know how to work with string bass. Because all he would do is pound all the time. Bam, bam, bam, bam, bam, bam. And no foot on the bass drumming. You suppose you hear that bass drum too. And they don't, and something else they don't do, they don't tune that bass drum. See, because they got keys on them bass drums, your tom-toms and all that. The man put them things there for you to tune them things.
But maybe he says you got to tune those out.
See, and you got to tune them. All drummers that I played with, they tune the snare drum, they tune all them drums. See, all instruments you got to tune.
I'll find different spokes when I was writing. I'll find the snare drums sound more like Kittle drums. Long time ago they used to sound like a bunch of shots. Yeah. A kid.
